content.title: Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir and Subsequent PCR Negativity in Patients With B-Cell Lymphoma and Prolonged SARS-CoV-2 PCR Positivity: A Case Series.
content.abstract: Prolonged SARS-CoV-2 PCR positivity is increasingly recognized in immunocompromised patients. We retrospectively analyzed four patients with B-cell lymphoma and prior anti-CD20 antibody therapy who exhibited prolonged PCR positivity after COVID-19 diagnosis. The median duration of PCR positivity was 57 days (range, 47-78 days); lymphoma treatment was interrupted in one patient and could not be resumed in another. Three patients received nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and became PCR negative 5-14 days after treatment initiation. These findings suggest that prolonged SARS-CoV-2 PCR positivity may disrupt lymphoma treatment and that PCR negativity was observed shortly after nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment in selected patients.

content.title: Metagenomic next-generation sequencing of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid unravels brucellosis in a patient with chronic lung disease and venous thrombosis: A case report.
content.abstract: BACKGROUND: Brucellosis is a re-emerging zoonosis in Xinjiang, China. Pulmonary involvement and thrombotic complications are rare but can be life-threatening. In patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF), unexplained respiratory worsening poses a diagnostic dilemma: is it an acute exacerbation of IPF, community-acquired pneumonia, or a zoonotic infection? We report a case of chronic brucellosis in an IPF patient who developed lower extremity venous thrombosis, diagnosed by metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF), thereby resolving the clinical dilemma. METHODS: A 57-year-old male farmer with IPF presented with progressive dyspnea and hypoxemia (SpO₂ 77% on room air). Serum Brucella agglutination test (SAT) and mNGS of BALF were performed. RESULTS: SAT was positive at 1:800. mNGS of BALF detected 191 reads of Brucella spp. Lower extremity ultrasound revealed left calf muscular venous thrombosis. He was treated with doxycycline, rifampicin, and rivaroxaban. At one-month follow-up, his dyspnea had improved, and no recurrent thrombosis occurred. CONCLUSION: In endemic areas, brucellosis should be considered in IPF patients with unexplained respiratory worsening, even without typical fever. mNGS of BALF is a valuable diagnostic tool when blood cultures are negative. Clinicians should also be aware that severe infection and hypoxemia are risk factors for venous thrombosis.

content.title: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis after Measles Outbreaks, the Philippines, 2007-2022.
content.abstract: Subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE) is a delayed, almost uniformly fatal complication of measles. The Philippines had measles outbreaks in 2010-2011, 2013, and 2018-2019; the last was the largest in the World Health Organization Western Pacific Region. Published SSPE data from the Philippines end in 2015. We reviewed all 20 children admitted with SSPE to a tertiary pediatric hospital in Quezon City during 2007-2022 and estimated year of measles infection. Median patient age was 6.2 years at hospital admission and 0.7 years at reported measles illness. Five (25.0%) of 20 admissions occurred in 2022, and estimated infection dates placed 4 patients within the 2018-2019 outbreak; all were admitted during 2020-2022. Given the multiyear latency of SSPE, additional cases might emerge over coming years. Reported measles history could not be established in one quarter of patients. Strengthened measles surveillance and sustained 2-dose vaccination coverage are needed.

content.title: Co-circulation of H5N1 and H5N6 high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses in migratory birds at a coastal wintering site in China.
content.abstract: Since 2020, H5Nx high pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (HPAIVs) belonging to hemagglutinin (HA) clade 2.3.4.4b have undergone widespread dispersal in wild birds, posing substantial threats to global poultry populations and mammals worldwide. In this study, we report the co-circulation of clade 2.3.4.4b H5N1 and H5N6 HPAIVs associated with mortality events in Anseriformes and Charadriiformes at a coastal wintering site in Fujian Province, China. H5N1 and H5N6 viruses were identified in four species of waterfowl (Bean Goose, Eastern Spot-billed Duck, Eurasian Wigeon, and Eurasian Curlew). Phylogenetic analysis indicated that these H5N1 and H5N6 isolates were clade 2.3.4.4b strains circulating within Eurasia and lacked known mammalian adaptation markers in key proteins. The infected birds exhibited severe systemic multi-organ pathology, with the most pronounced damage observed in the lungs. H5N6 and H5N1 viruses caused lethal injury in BALB/c mice, with H5N1 leading to systemic infection. Environmental sampling also revealed the presence of H5N1 HPAIVs alongside low-pathogenicity avian influenza viruses (LPAIVs) such as H3N1 and H6N1. Our findings highlight the complex and dynamic transmission patterns of H5 HPAIV in wild bird populations and the substantial threat they pose to mammals, underscoring the critical importance of sustained surveillance for high pathogenicity avian influenza in wild birds.

content.title: Chikungunya case cluster with nonspecific symptoms: implications for primary care in Switzerland.
content.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early clinical presentation of chikungunya fever and other arbovirus infections is often nonspecific, potentially delaying diagnosis, particularly in settings where these diseases are less frequently considered. Competent vectors are expanding in Switzerland, increasing the risk of autochthonous arbovirus transmission. CASE SERIES: We report seven cases in a group of travellers returning from Kenya in summer 2025. All patients presented with fever, arthralgia affecting the small joints of the hands and feet, nausea, diarrhoea, and rash. Additional symptoms included generalised lymphadenopathy and peripheral oedema. Initial diagnostic tests were inconclusive, with negative results on rapid diagnostic tests for chikungunya antibodies, dengue antibodies, and malaria antigen. The definitive diagnosis was established after 35 days following the emergence of chikungunya IgG and IgM antibodies. DISCUSSION: The presentation resembled a nonspecific febrile illness. Repeated, appropriately timed laboratory testing was necessary to establish the diagnosis. Early diagnostic results may be misleading, particularly when testing methods are not selected appropriately for the stage of the disease. With competent mosquito vectors established in Switzerland, imported cases present a risk of local transmission. Severe infections and persistent joint pain may lead to long-term disability. CONCLUSION: Primary care doctors should consider chikungunya fever in returning travellers and, during the mosquito-active season, in non-travellers in areas with established competent vectors. Patients may present with symptoms ranging from nonspecific febrile illness to more typical manifestations of chikungunya, including fever, arthralgia of the small joints, and rash. Appropriate test selection, timing, and repeated testing when indicated are essential for accurate diagnosis, management, and documentation of the disease.

content.title: Postmortem Artifacts Caused by Freshwater Crab Scavenging on Human Remains in Sri Lanka: A Case Series.
content.abstract: Artifacts from aquatic animal scavenging can disfigure human remains, making identification difficult, obscuring or mimicking antemortem injuries, and destroying evidence. Although freshwater crabs are common scavengers in tropical freshwater, literature describing their effects on human remains is limited. This case series describes postmortem scavenging by the freshwater crabs Oziotelphusa ceylonensis and Ceylonthelphusa rugosa in Sri Lanka, highlighting their forensic significance. Three adult males who died in separate incidents of accidental drowning were recovered from shallow freshwater streams in Sri Lanka. Freshwater crabs were observed scavenging on the bodies at the scene or recovered with the bodies during autopsy. The lesions consisted of superficial soft-tissue defects on the eyelids, lips, nose, ears, neck, chest, feet, and external genitalia. The injuries lacked vital reaction and were oval, elongated, or irregular in shape with scalloped margins and crater-like appearances, exposing underlying subcutaneous tissues or muscles. Internal examinations were consistent with drowning. Collected crab specimens were morphologically identified as Oziotelphusa ceylonensis in 2 cases and Ceylonthelphusa rugosa in one case. Freshwater crabs can produce characteristic postmortem artifacts that may mask or mimic antemortem injuries. Recognition of these artifacts is important for expressing accurate medico-legal opinions in cases involving human remains recovered from freshwater environments.

content.title: An outbreak of H7N7 high pathogenicity avian influenza in Victoria, Australia, in 2020.
content.abstract: On 31 July 2020, an outbreak of H7N7 high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) was confirmed on a free-range, egg-producing poultry farm in the Lethbridge area of southwest Victoria. The property was immediately quarantined, and an emergency animal disease response plan was prepared to guide containment, and then eradication, of the disease in accordance with the Australian Veterinary Emergency Plan (AUSVETPLAN) and to meet the requirements of the Australian Emergency Animal Disease Response Agreement (EADRA). Birds on two additional premises were subsequently confirmed as infected with H7N7 HPAI. Extensive surveillance undertaken during the response also identified infection with low pathogenicity avian influenza on three further properties-two commercial turkey properties (H5N2 subtype) and one emu farm (H7N6 subtype). These properties were also subjected to disease eradication procedures. Humane destruction of birds on all affected properties was completed by 8 September 2020. Cleaning and decontamination activities were completed on all sites by 11 December 2020. Extensive tracing and surveillance activities did not identify any further cases of H7N7 HPAI in domestic or wild birds. In terms of both numbers of birds and impacted properties, this was the largest outbreak of HPAI recorded in Australia up to that time. On 26 February 2021, Australia's Chief Veterinary Officer declared that the country had regained freedom from HPAI in accordance with international standards published by the World Organisation for Animal Health (then the OIE).

content.title: An Unusual Mechanism of Stroke in Neurobrucellosis: Middle Cerebral Artery Infarction Secondary to Direct Abscess Compression - A Case Report and Literature Review.
content.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Brucellosis is a zoonotic infection that remains endemic across the Middle East, Central Asia, the Mediterranean basin, and parts of Africa and Latin America. Neurobrucellosis (NB) develops in fewer than 5% of cases and constitutes the most severe systemic complication. Cerebrovascular involvement is uncommon and most often attributed to small-vessel vasculitis, immune-mediated endarteritis, or septic embolization. Ischemic stroke caused by direct mechanical compression of an intracranial artery by a Brucella abscess has not been previously reported. CASE PRESENTATION: A 47-year-old previously healthy male with occupational livestock exposure presented with sudden onset of left-sided weakness, facial droop, and global aphasia. Initial imaging demonstrated an acute right middle cerebral artery (MCA) territory infarct, and standard ischemic stroke management was initiated. Over the next 24 h, intermittent low-grade fever, persistent confusion, and focal motor seizures emerged despite levetiracetam. Subsequent magnetic resonance imaging showed a 2.5 cm rim-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with central diffusion restriction, consistent with a pyogenic abscess. Magnetic resonance angiography demonstrated focal occlusion of the anterior segment of the right MCA, immediately adjacent to the abscess. Cerebrospinal fluid showed lymphocytic pleocytosis (36 cells/mm3, 85% lymphocytes) and elevated protein (112 mg/dL). Serum Brucella IgG returned positive on day 20, confirming neurobrucellosis. Triple antimicrobial therapy with intravenous ceftriaxone, oral doxycycline, and oral rifampicin produced gradual neurological improvement, and the patient was discharged on long-term oral therapy. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates a novel cerebrovascular mechanism in NB, in which mass effect from a peri-vascular abscess produced ischemic stroke. Coexisting perilesional inflammation likely contributed through a vasculitic component, and the two mechanisms are not mutually exclusive. The absence of systemic brucellosis features delayed recognition and underscores the protean clinical presentation of NB. Brucellosis warrants consideration in the differential diagnosis of acute ischemic stroke when imaging reveals concurrent intracranial infectious lesions, particularly in endemic regions. Early antimicrobial therapy is critical to limit progression and improve neurological outcomes.

content.title: Temporal Trends in Invasive Pulmonary Aspergillosis Among Critically Ill Patients: Serum Galactomannan Testing Intensity and Host Risk Status.
content.abstract: OBJECTIVES: We evaluated temporal trends in invasive pulmonary aspergillosis (IPA) incidence in relation to serum galactomannan (GM) testing intensity and compared outcomes by classical host-risk status. METHODS: Adults with ICU stays ≥72 hours during 2017-2024 were retrospectively screened for proven/probable IPA. Consensus EORTC/MSGERC and FUNDICU definitions defined the primary cohort. Modified criteria were exploratory. Negative binomial and Cox regression assessed incidence and 30-day mortality. RESULTS: Among 11,707 ICU stays, 135 patients met consensus definitions; 55 (40.7%) lacked classical host risk factors, rising to 48.9% under modified criteria. IPA incidence increased over time (IRR/year 1.40; 95% CI 1.06-1.85). After adjustment for serum GM testing intensity, the calendar-year IRR was 0.73 (95% CI 0.54-0.98), whereas testing intensity was strongly associated with measured incidence (IRR 6.15; 95% CI 2.81-13.43). Patients without classical host risk factors received antifungal therapy less often (12.7% vs 67.5%) and had higher crude 30-day mortality (58.2% vs 36.2%). The adjusted host-status association was attenuated (aHR 1.48; 95% CI 0.82-2.66). CONCLUSIONS: The temporal rise in measured IPA incidence was associated with serum GM testing intensity, underscoring diagnostic ascertainment. Patients without classical host risk factors were treated less often and had higher mortality, although the adjusted association was attenuated.

content.title: Impact of COVID-19 restrictions on emergency bellwether procedures in South and Southeast Asia.
content.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Around the time COVID-19 was declared a global pandemic, various restrictions and measures were implemented at all levels to limit disease spread and preserve healthcare capacity. Data are lacking in many low- and middle-income countries on how these measures impact healthcare utilisation and outcomes. This study aims to determine the impact of COVID-19 restrictions on volumes of the three emergency bellwether procedures in South and Southeast Asia. METHODS: This was an interrupted time series study of patients who underwent any of the three emergency bellwether procedures (caesarean section, laparotomy and open fracture fixation) from 1 January 2018 to 31 December 2021 at one of eight institutions in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, India and Vietnam. We compared the weekly volumes, baseline characteristics and outcomes of each procedure across different time periods in each institution defined by different levels of COVID-19 restrictions using selected indicators from a city-level and hospital-level response index. RESULTS: Weekly volumes of emergency caesarean section decreased significantly in Guwahati Neurological Research Centre (GNRC) (p=1.62×10-5) and Ulin General Hospital (UGH) (p<2.2×10-16) but increased in Adam Malik Hospital (AMH) (p=1.45×10-5). For laparotomies, volume increased in Singapore General Hospital (p=2.38×10-5) but decreased in Military Hospital 175 (p=6.30×10-7). The volume of open fracture fixations decreased in GNRC (p=3.08×10-8), AMH (p=1.68×10-6) and UGH (p=8.15×10-6). CONCLUSIONS: COVID-19 restrictions on the city and hospital level were associated with a decrease in surgical volumes of the three bellwether procedures in some of the institutions. There was some suggestion of surgical capacity limitations in UGH and Military Hospital 175 during periods of more stringent COVID-19 restrictions.

content.title: The medical and surgery outcomes of pulmonary hydatid cyst disease: A 12-year multidisciplinary experience.
content.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hydatid cyst disease (PHCD) remains a significant public health problem in endemic regions. AIMS: To evaluate the demographic, serological, radiological, and surgical characteristics of patients with PHCD and to identify factors associated with hepatic involvement and postoperative outcomes. METHODS: This retrospective study included 515 consecutive patients who underwent surgical treatment for PHCD at Dicle University Faculty of Medicine between 2013 and 2025. Demographic characteristics, cyst features, indirect fluorescent antibody (IFA) test results, concomitant hepatic involvement, surgical procedures, postoperative outcomes, and complications were analyzed. RESULTS: Among 515 patients, 275 (53.4%) were male and 240 (46.6%) were female. Female patients were significantly older than male patients (28.0 ± 18.0 vs. 23.8 ± 18.4 years, p = 0.002). Hepatic involvement was significantly associated with positive IFA test results (p < 0.001), bilateral pulmonary disease (p < 0.001), multiple pulmonary cysts (p < 0.001), female sex (p = 0.045), and left-sided pulmonary involvement (p = 0.019). Blood group distribution was not associated with hepatic involvement (p = 0.773), although IFA positivity differed significantly among ABO blood groups (p = 0.006). Larger cyst size was associated with longer hospital stay (r = 0.130, p = 0.003) and prolonged drainage duration (r = 0.094, p = 0.034). Perforated cysts were associated with increased hospital stay (r = 0.180, p < 0.001) and drainage duration (r = 0.139, p = 0.002). Pediatric patients had significantly larger cysts than adults (p = 0.007). CONCLUSIONS: Positive IFA results, multiple pulmonary cysts, and bilateral lung involvement are associated with concomitant hepatic hydatid disease. Cyst size and perforation status significantly influence postoperative recovery, particularly hospital stay and drainage duration. Surgical treatment provides excellent outcomes with low reoperation rates and no disease-related mortality in experienced centers.

content.title: Uveitis following COVID-19 Infection: A Case Series including Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada Disease and Birdshot Chorioretinopathy.
content.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Uveitis in the context of COVID-19 is rare, yet a relatively higher frequency of uncommon posterior variants has been described both following COVID-19 infection and after COVID-19 vaccination. In this series, we report 4 cases of new-onset uveitis following a PCR-confirmed COVID-19 infection: 2 cases of incomplete Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada (VKH) disease and 2 cases of birdshot chorioretinopathy (BSCR). CASE PRESENTATIONS: Four patients presented with ocular symptoms and characteristic clinical findings consistent with either VKH disease or BSCR shortly after PCR-confirmed COVID-19 infection. VKH disease and BSCR occurred within 2 weeks of infection and 1 month after infection, respectively. Human leukocyte antigen (HLA) genotyping revealed HLA-A29 in both BSCR cases. One VKH case carried the HLA-DRB1*04:04 allele, indicating possible genetic susceptibility. No relevant medical history was reported, and systemic work-up was negative in all cases. CONCLUSION: We report the first 2 cases of BSCR in the setting of PCR-confirmed COVID-19 infection, and add 2 cases of COVID-19-associated VKH disease to the existing literature. These observations further support the hypothesis that viral infections may trigger autoimmune uveitic entities. While causality remains to be fully established, COVID-19 should be considered a potential immunological trigger for BSCR, in line with its documented role in VKH disease. Further studies are needed to elucidate the potential role of viral infections in the pathogenesis of BSCR.

content.title: Severe Inflammatory Response and Moderate Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) in an Immunocompetent Patient With Disseminated Tuberculosis: A Case Report.
content.abstract: An acute exacerbation in some tuberculosis (TB) cases can lead to widespread infection; this disseminated disease may progress when the body's immune response becomes dysregulated. Although rare, certain patients without obvious immune compromise can develop severe organ dysfunction if inflammation escalates uncontrollably. Respiratory failure can develop rapidly once lung tissue becomes overwhelmed by excessive inflammatory signaling. This presentation is uncommon but severe and is frequently unrecognized in its early stages because symptoms mimic other critical conditions. Mortality increases substantially once acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) develops in the setting of disseminated infection. A 40-year-old man, previously in good health, presented with severe respiratory distress. Oxygen saturation declined rapidly, requiring urgent endotracheal intubation. He subsequently required vasopressor support and prone positioning due to advanced respiratory failure. Laboratory evaluation revealed thrombocytopenia and elevated liver enzymes. Comprehensive microbiological testing did not identify common viral, bacterial, or fungal pathogens. A positive Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) PCR result from bronchial fluid confirmed disseminated TB. His clinical course was complicated by moderate ARDS and a hyperinflammatory state, consistent with an exaggerated immune response to TB. Treatment was initiated with rifampin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol (RIPE) therapy along with systemic corticosteroids (methylprednisolone 40 mg every eight hours). Clinical improvement was observed, and ventilatory support was discontinued following targeted treatment. The patient was discharged with a plan for prolonged anti-tubercular therapy. This case illustrates how disseminated TB can trigger a severe inflammatory response leading to moderate ARDS, even in the absence of underlying immunosuppression. Early recognition of this presentation is critical, and combined treatment with antimicrobial therapy and immunomodulation may improve outcomes.

content.title: Virological and epidemiological investigations of a severe hand foot and mouth disease outbreak, Vietnam, 2023.
content.abstract: We report on the virological and epidemiological features of a severe hand foot and mouth disease outbreak in Vietnam in 2023. Enterovirus A71 (EV-A71) subgenogroup B5, first emerging around November 2022, and imported into Vietnam through a single introduction, was the primary cause. Convalescent plasma collected from patients infected with subgenogroups B5 in 2014 and 2023 could neutralize both contemporary viruses with comparable titers, suggesting no evidence of immune evasion. However, at one and six months before the start of the outbreak, only 6.7% of 0- < 3 year-old children in Ho Chi Minh City, an epicenter of the outbreak, had neutralizing antibodies against EV-A71. Seroprevalence increased as the outbreak progressed, coinciding with a drop in EV-A71 infected patients residing in Ho Chi Minh City, suggesting that serosurveillance could be a useful tool to assess the risk of pathogen emergence. Our collective findings have provided novel insights into the epidemiological factors driving EV-A71 emergence, and therefore would inform outbreak preparedness and response, and in particular the development of serosurveillance-based approach to assess the risk of pathogen emergence. EV-A71 infection represents an ongoing public health threat, currently affecting countries in the Asia-Pacific region, but with a high potential to become a global problem, and therefore should be closely monitored.

content.title: Case Report: mNGS-negative Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome with small bowel obstruction as the initial manifestation in a glucocorticoid-exposed COPD patient: a fatal case.
content.abstract: BACKGROUND: Strongyloides hyperinfection syndrome (SHS) is a life-threatening condition in immunocompromised hosts with an extremely high mortality rate. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) demonstrates limited sensitivity for parasitic detection, and its clinical value remains to be fully elucidated. The conventional microscopy remains an indispensable tool for the diagnosis of parasitic infections. CASE DESCRIPTION: A 73-year-old male patient with a history of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and cerebral infarction presented with abdominal pain and distension for 7 days and no bowel movement for 3 days. He was diagnosed with incomplete small bowel obstruction at an outside hospital and treated with fasting, enemas, meropenem, and methylprednisolone. He was subsequently transferred to our hospital due to acute lower respiratory tract infection. Chest radiography revealed bilateral diffuse infiltrates, and his condition rapidly deteriorated, requiring admission to the intensive care unit (ICU), endotracheal intubation, mechanical ventilation, and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT). Stool smear and retrospective sputum examination both identified larvae of Strongyloides stercoralis. However, mNGS of sputum and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) obtained upon admission failed to detect any parasitic sequences. The patient was treated sequentially with albendazole and ivermectin, in combination with broad-spectrum antibacterial, antifungal, and antiviral therapy. He ultimately died on February 11, 2025, due to severe pneumonia, sepsis, and bone marrow suppression. CONCLUSION: For immunocompromised hosts with multiple risk factors, particularly those exposed to glucocorticoids, active parasitic microscopic examination of stool and respiratory secretions should be pursued when unexplained pulmonary infiltrates coexist with gastrointestinal symptoms, even in the setting of negative mNGS results, to avoid missed diagnosis.

content.title: Case Report: Bacteremic respiratory tularemia causing refractory ARDS requiring VV-ECMO.
content.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory tularemia is a rare but potentially serious manifestation of Francisella tularensis infection. We report a rare case of bacteremic respiratory tularemia complicated by refractory acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) requiring veno-venous extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VV-ECMO), highlighting the diagnostic challenges and therapeutic implications of this uncommon presentation. CASE PRESENTATION: A 78-year-old man developed severe pneumonia following river water aspiration after a bicycle accident. After transient initial improvement, he experienced progressive respiratory deterioration despite broad-spectrum antimicrobial treatment, ultimately developing refractory ARDS requiring invasive mechanical ventilation, prone positioning and VV-ECMO. Three consecutive sets of blood cultures revealed the presence of Francisella tularensis, whereas bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) cultures remained negative. No extrapulmonary manifestations of tularemia were identified. Targeted antimicrobial therapy with ciprofloxacin and gentamicin was initiated but failed to prevent a fatal outcome. CONCLUSION: Respiratory tularemia should be considered in patients with severe pneumonia following environmental exposure, particularly when respiratory status deteriorates despite broad-spectrum β-lactam therapy. Repeated blood cultures may establish the diagnosis despite negative BAL cultures. Early recognition and prompt initiation of effective antimicrobial therapy are essential, as β-lactam antibiotics are clinically ineffective against F. tularensis. This case also illustrates the potential severity of respiratory tularemia, which may progress to refractory ARDS requiring VV-ECMO.

content.title: Cardiac injury in children with severe hand, foot and mouth disease: risk factors and clinical outcomes.
content.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine the risk factors and clinical outcomes of cardiac injury in pediatric patients with severe hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD). METHODS: We conducted a multicenter retrospective study at two tertiary children's hospitals in southern Vietnam, including hospitalized patients with severe HFMD and suspected cardiovascular complications. Cardiac injury was identified according to cardiac enzyme results and findings from electrocardiography and echocardiography. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify risk factors associated with cardiac injury. RESULTS: A total of 395 patients were included, with a male predominance, and 96.5% were younger than 36 months. Typical skin rash and herpangina remained the most common clinical manifestations. Intensive care unit admission was required in 72.2% of cases, and 50.9% required endotracheal intubation with mechanical ventilation. Cardiac injury was identified in 7.3% (29/395) of severe HFMD cases with suspected cardiovascular complications. Fever ≥ 39 °C (aOR 10.5, 95% CI 3.4-32.6, p 20 mg/L (aOR 3.3, 95% CI 1.3-8.4, p = 0.012), and aspartate aminotransferase > 40 U/L (aOR 4.1, 95% CI 1.7-9.8, p = 0.002) were independent risk factors for cardiac injury. Patients with cardiac injury had higher mortality, longer hospital stays, and a greater incidence of neurological sequelae compared with those without cardiac injury. CONCLUSIONS: Cardiac injury in pediatric patients with severe HFMD is associated with adverse clinical outcomes, underscoring the need for early risk stratification and comprehensive cardiac assessment.

content.title: Reassortment of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza as a Driver for Zoonotic Spillover, Asia.
content.abstract: Highly pathogenic avian influenza H5Nx viruses remain a major zoonotic threat, yet global attention has focused largely on clade 2.3.4.4b, potentially overlooking major changes within long-endemic H5N1 lineages in Asia. Recent reports from South and Southeast Asia describe the emergence of reassortant clade 2.3.2.1 viruses alongside renewed human infections after apparent prolonged epidemiologic stability. Collectively, those events suggest a regional pattern rather than isolated anomalies. In this article, we argue that reassortment, rather than point mutation alone, might be an underrecognized driver of zoonotic risk in endemic H5N1 lineages and is reshaping those lineages. We examine why such events might be underrecognized in settings with entrenched poultry influenza, identify limitations of current surveillance systems, and call for integrated, real-time approaches linking genomic detection with phenotypic assessment across animal and human health sectors to enable timely risk assessment and coordinated public health action.

content.title: Case Report: Liangxue Jiedu Huayu Formula as adjunctive therapy for leptospirosis with Weil's syndrome.
content.abstract: BACKGROUND: Leptospirosis is a global zoonotic disease with over one million cases annually worldwide. Approximately 5%-10% of patients progress to Weil's syndrome, characterized by multi-organ failure and high mortality, but treatment options remain limited. This report describes a patient with severe leptospirosis who showed marked improvement following treatment with Liangxue Jiedu Huayu Formula (LXJDHYF), a traditional Chinese medicine formula, and explores potential mechanisms. CASE PRESENTATION: A 54-year-old male farmer developed high fever, jaundice, acute kidney injury, and early disseminated intravascular coagulation after working in a lotus pond. Leptospirosis was confirmed by a four-fold rise in MAT titer from 1:50 to 1:200. Despite initial treatment with conventional therapies including antibiotics, continuous renal replacement therapy, and plasma infusion, the patient remained febrile with persistently elevated white blood cell and bilirubin levels. From day 5 of hospitalization, LXJDHYF was added. Fever gradually subsided, total bilirubin progressively decreased, serum creatinine eventually normalized, and coagulation function returned to normal. At 6-month follow-up, the patient had fully recovered. MECHANISTIC EXPLORATION: Network pharmacology identified 14 common targets, including ICAM1, SELE, TLR4, and SERPINE1. KEGG enrichment revealed pathways related to TLR4/NF-κB signaling, cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction, and complement/coagulation cascades. Molecular docking showed strong binding affinities (≤ -7.0 kcal/mol) between core components (cryptotanshinone, nortanshinone, rhein, naringenin) and core targets (TLR4, ICAM1, ALB). These computational findings are hypothesis-generating and require experimental validation. CONCLUSION: This case suggests that adjuvant treatment with LXJDHYF may be beneficial for leptospirosis complicated by Weil's syndrome, based on conventional therapy. Network pharmacology has generated testable hypotheses regarding multi-target modulation of inflammatory, adhesion, and coagulation pathways. These computational findings require experimental validation.

content.title: Nowcasting officially reported highly pathogenic avian influenza outbreak counts under heterogeneous reporting delays.
content.abstract: Official animal disease series are often incomplete due to delays in reporting. This retrospective observational study evaluated whether increased model complexity enhances probabilistic nowcasts of eventual officially reported outbreak-equivalent counts. We reconstructed historical information states from a fixed extraction from the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) World Animal Health Information System (WAHIS), which included 46,860 highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) and 72,690 African swine fever (ASF) outbreaks. Twelve prespecified methods were assessed over 78 locked cutoffs for 2024-2025 using the Weighted Interval Score (WIS), calibration diagnostics, block bootstrap, simulation, and a separately frozen USDA APHIS transfer evaluation. The primary HPAI analysis included 35,880 observations from 115 country-host units. At week closure, only 7.6% of eventual HPAI and 6.7% of ASF outbreak equivalents were visible, with completeness varying by host, region, year, season, and workload. The prespecified primary hypothesis was not supported: the delay-aware temporal network scored 6.9% worse than the hierarchical Bayesian comparator, and the relational graph changed WIS by only 0.4%. Gradient-boosted quantile regression improved WIS by 18.5% (absolute difference -0.0397, 95% interval -0.0553 to -0.0255), but the improvement reached 26.0% among high-volume reporters and reversed to a 6.3% deficit among units with minimal reporting history. Conditioning on the partial count was 24.7% worse than a matched no-delay network at cohort age 0 and performed better thereafter. The slower-reporting ASF system reversed the pooled contrast, whereas the APHIS module improved WIS by 10.1% after system-specific retraining. Adding an explicit mass at zero enhanced the transparent comparator by 18.8% and resulted in no detectable difference from gradient boosting; the neural model remained 17.4% worse under the same recalibration. In exploratory analyses, gradient boosting cleared the prespecified 5% gate under all six cohort definitions and all three maturity horizons. Performance deteriorated markedly for high-volume countries and regions excluded from training. These estimates pertain to eventual officially reported outbreak equivalents under the surveillance conditions studied, not undetected infections.

content.title: Ischemic stroke after bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination and influenza vaccination during the 2022-2023 season: a multi-site self-controlled case series study.
content.abstract: BACKGROUND: The Vaccine Safety Datalink (VSD) detected a statistical signal for ischemic events (ischemic stroke or transient ischemic attack) following bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination through prospective surveillance during 2022-2023. Although multiple studies from other surveillance systems and countries reported no increased risk, important methodological limitations remained. This U.S. study addressed those limitations by evaluating the ischemic stroke risk following bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination, influenza vaccination, and their same-day coadministration using an event-dependent self-controlled case series (SCCS) design. METHODS: Study outcomes included first-ever ischemic stroke (primary outcome), first-in-1-year ischemic stroke (secondary outcome), and ischemic events (exploratory outcomes), identified using ICD-10-CM codes in inpatient and emergency department settings during September 1, 2022-March 31, 2023, among individuals aged ≥12 years across eight VSD sites. Analyses were conducted separately for Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna bivalent vaccines, with relative incidences (RI) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) estimated for 1-21-day and 1-42-day risk intervals, using person-time outside these intervals as the control period. Subgroup analyses were performed by age group (12-64, ≥65 years) and history of documented SARS-CoV-2 infection. RESULTS: A total of 6510 first-ever ischemic strokes were identified among more than 6.8 million participants. Among recipients of Pfizer-BioNTech bivalent COVID-19 and influenza vaccines, no statistically significant increased risk of first-ever ischemic stroke was observed following bivalent COVID-19 vaccination (RI = 0.94; 95% CI: 0.63-1.41), influenza vaccination (RI = 0.95; 95% CI: 0.82-1.10), or same-day coadministration (RI = 1.15; 95% CI: 0.88-1.49) within 1-21-day risk intervals; findings were similar for 1-42-day intervals. Comparable null results were observed for Moderna vaccine and across all subgroups, secondary, and exploratory outcomes. CONCLUSION: No increased risk of ischemic stroke was found following bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccination, influenza vaccination, or their coadministration in this multi-site SCCS study. These findings are consistent with previous studies and underscore the importance of continued vaccine safety monitoring.

content.title: Three-Phase Decline in Reported Farm-Level Fowl Typhoid Occurrence in the Republic of Korea, 2000-2024: Temporal Alignment with the 2016-2017 H5N6 HPAI Epidemic.
content.abstract: This study characterized the long-term changes in reported farm-level fowl typhoid occurrence in the Republic of Korea from 2000 to 2024. Farm-level notification records (n = 1495) were obtained from the national livestock disease database. Annual counts were analyzed on a log(count + 1) scale using segmented linear regression. The number of breakpoints was selected by Bayesian information criterion (BIC) comparison of candidate segmented models, and BIC favored a two-breakpoint model. Breakpoints were estimated at 2009.0 (95% CI, 2004.7-2013.3) and 2016.5 (95% CI, 2014.1-2019.0). Phase 1 (2000-2009) declined significantly (annual percent change [APC], -16.3%; 95% CI, -25.9 to -5.5), Phase 2 (2009-2016) showed no significant change (APC, 3.7%; 95% CI, -10.3 to 20.0), and Phase 3 (2016-2024) showed an accelerated decline (APC, -28.0%; 95% CI, -34.9 to -19.8). Province-specific post-2016 slopes were not associated with cumulative provincial HPAI events during 2014-2024 (Spearman's ρ = -0.143, p = 0.736). The post-2016 acceleration temporally overlapped with the 2016-2017 H5N6 HPAI epidemic, but the study did not measure the contemporaneous interventions or denominators needed for causal attribution.

content.title: Klebsiella pneumoniae pyogenic liver abscess mimicking hepatic malignancy in a non-diabetic patient: A case report from Kazakhstan.
content.abstract: Pyogenic liver abscess is an infectious condition associated with significant morbidity and mortality, with Klebsiella pneumoniae emerging as a major pathogen. We report a case of Klebsiella pneumoniae pyogenic liver abscess in a 76-year-old woman from Kazakhstan, representing one of the first indexed reports from Central Asia. The patient presented with prolonged fever, jaundice, and constitutional symptoms without diabetes mellitus. Initial ultrasound revealed a large heterogeneous hepatic mass with a solid, tumor-like appearance, raising concern for malignancy in the setting of chronic hepatitis B infection. MRI and contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated diffusion restriction, multiloculated architecture, and mild peripheral and septal enhancement without arterial hyperenhancement or venous washout, favoring hepatic abscess over hepatocellular carcinoma. The solid, tumor-like ultrasound appearance, atypical for a pyogenic abscess in its resemblance to hepatic malignancy, posed the primary diagnostic challenge, underscoring the value of multimodal imaging in characterizing hepatic lesions. Additionally, KPLA should be considered in the differential diagnosis even in the absence of classical metabolic risk factors and in regions with limited epidemiological data.

content.title: Genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance for monitoring human norovirus GII circulation.
content.abstract: Norovirus GII causes a substantial global burden of acute gastroenteritis, and genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance offers a complementary approach for monitoring community circulation beyond cases captured by routine clinical surveillance. We monitored four municipal wastewater treatment plants in Beijing, China, from October 2023 to September 2024 and compared weekly GII genotype profiles with contemporaneous sporadic-case and outbreak surveillance. Strict-weekly genotype comparisons were the primary inference and used moving-block bootstrap confidence intervals, block-sign tests, and false-discovery-rate correction; centred 3-week profiles were used for description and sensitivity analysis. Bray-Curtis dissimilarity quantified compositional concordance, and same-week and lagged Spearman correlations compared wastewater GII concentration with clinical surveillance activity. In the centred 3-week wastewater series, GII.4 had the highest mean read-based relative abundance (31.1%), followed by GII.17 (17.5%) and GII.7 (15.2%). In strict-weekly comparisons, wastewater had lower GII.17 representation than sporadic cases (-32.6 percentage points) and lower GII.7 representation than outbreaks (-14.0 percentage points). Wastewater had higher GII.3, GII.4, GII.6, and GII.9 representation than sporadic cases and higher GII.9 and GII.13 representation than outbreaks; the GII.4 and GII.7 differences were sensitive to analytical specification, and the GII.13 effect was small. Mean strict-weekly Bray-Curtis dissimilarities were 0.590-0.679 in 32 common weeks. Same-week and lagged wastewater concentration correlations with sporadic-case positivity and outbreak case counts were not significant after temporal-dependence and multiplicity correction. Genotype-resolved wastewater surveillance documented co-circulating GII genotypes and recurrent source-specific differences, while read-based relative abundance remained dependent on catchment coverage and genotype-specific analytical performance.

content.title: Leukoreduction by Manual Exchange Transfusion Versus Leukapheresis in the Management of Critical Pertussis in Children: A Case Series.
content.abstract: BACKGROUND: Marked leukocytosis in critical pertussis is a major predictor of mortality in young infants, with reported mortality rates of 40-85%. Although leukoreduction is frequently performed in critical pertussis with marked leukocytosis using either whole blood exchange transfusion or therapeutic leukapheresis, no evidence-based guidelines exist, and published data remain limited to small case reports. We present a descriptive case series evaluating the feasibility, hematologic response, and short-term outcomes of leukoreduction using these two modalities. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective case series of five children aged 3-52 weeks with PCR-confirmed pertussis having marked leukocytosis admitted to a tertiary pediatric intensive care unit between February and July 2024. Leukoreduction was performed following multidisciplinary consensus. Absolute and percentage reductions in white blood cell (WBC) counts were calculated using pre- and post-procedure values. Clinical characteristics, illness severity scores (PRISM, PELOD, PIM3), leukoreduction modality, and procedural complications were reviewed. RESULTS: Median WBC count decreased from 58 × 10⁹/L (range, 33-81.6) before the procedure to 18 × 10⁹/L (range, 13-41) after the procedure, representing a median reduction of 64.1% (range, 38.1-75.8%). In this case series, exchange transfusion was associated with a greater median WBC reduction compared with leukapheresis (71.4% vs. 56.8%). However, exchange transfusion resulted in a more pronounced median reduction in platelet count (79.9% vs. 44.7%) and a greater increase in hemoglobin (mean increase, 5.5 g/dL vs. 0.47 g/dL). CONCLUSION: In this case series, leukoreduction was feasible and produced immediate cytoreduction in critically ill infants with pertussis-associated hyperleukocytosis. Exchange transfusion was associated with greater WBC reduction but more pronounced platelet depletion. Larger multicenter studies are needed to further evaluate these modalities and guide modality selection and timing.

content.title: Detection of highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) virus, clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype B3.13 in placentas from aborted bovine fetuses.
content.abstract: Infection by highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) A(H5N1) virus (family Orthomyxoviridae, taxon species Alphainfluenzavirus influenzae), clade 2.3.4.4b, genotype B3.13, was first diagnosed in dairy cattle in the United States in March 2024. Here, we present a cluster of bovine abortions in whose placentas HPAI A(H5N1) was detected. Only placentas were submitted in all 5 cases received. Grossly, 3 placentas had multifocal edema; no significant gross abnormalities were observed in the other 2 placentas. Microscopically, one placenta had random areas of mineralization and another placenta had mild neutrophilic placentitis. Reverse-transcription quantitative real-time PCR for influenza A virus and avian influenza A virus subtype H5N1 were positive in all 5 placentas. RNAscope in-situ hybridization for matrix protein gene was positive in one placenta. Routine ancillary tests for bovine abortion diagnostic work-up did not detect any other abortifacient pathogens. We speculate that abortion was caused by the HPAI A(H5N1) virus.

content.title: Repeated detection of West Nile virus in Aedes caspius during an unusually early transmission season in humans in northern Italy, 2026.
content.abstract: In Lombardy, northern Italy, 2026, the first neuroinvasive West Nile virus (WNV) human case was reported on 7 July. Concurrently, high abundances of Aedes caspius and low numbers of Culex pipiens occurred at several surveillance sites. Testing seven archived Ae. caspius pools collected in July revealed WNV lineage 2 in six pools from three independent sites. A virus sequence from Ae. caspius shared > 99.94% nt identity with contemporaneous human-derived sequences. Further investigating possible Ae. caspius vector competence, particularly for WNV lineage 2, is warranted.

content.title: Infection prevention and control considerations in invasive group A streptococcus outbreaks.
content.abstract: Invasive Streptococcus pyogenes (group A streptococcus, GAS) infection is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality and has shown a notable resurgence in several countries since late 2022, including the United Kingdom (UK) and Ireland. Healthcare-associated cases, particularly in maternity and acute hospital settings, present significant infection prevention and control (IPC) challenges due to the organism's high transmissibility, potential for asymptomatic carriage among patients and healthcare workers, and the rapid progression of invasive disease. Even a single healthcare-associated case may signal unrecognised transmission within the clinical environment and therefore requires prompt investigation. This IPC Toolkit article summarises practical approaches to recognising, investigating, and managing GAS outbreaks in acute healthcare settings. Current UK guidance from the UK Health Security Agency and the British Infection Association is reviewed alongside recent outbreak reports and emerging evidence relevant to hospital practice. Key operational considerations include early case recognition, structured outbreak management through an incident management team, epidemiological investigation, and microbiological characterisation of isolates, including the use of whole genome sequencing to establish transmission pathways. The article also discusses patient isolation, environmental control measures, healthcare worker screening, and the role of targeted chemoprophylaxis for high-risk contacts. Recent literature emphasises the growing role of genomic epidemiology in outbreak confirmation and highlights the operational challenges associated with healthcare worker screening and contact management. Emerging population-level data may also influence future approaches to chemoprophylaxis for contacts. This article provides a practical framework to support clinicians and IPC teams in responding effectively to suspected or confirmed healthcare-associated GAS outbreaks.

content.title: Case Report: Henoch-Schönlein-like purpura as an unusual presentation of acute hepatitis E virus infection.
content.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection is increasingly recognized as a cause of extrahepatic manifestations; however, cutaneous purpuric manifestations are exceptionally rare, with only one previous case of Henoch-Schönlein purpura (HSP) reported in association with acute HEV infection. METHODS: This study describes the case of a 91-year-old man admitted with palpable purpura of the lower limbs, associated with jaundice, hypertransaminasemia, and cholestatic abnormalities. Molecular and serological assays were performed. RESULTS: Serological testing showed anti-HEV IgM and IgG positivity, and HEV RNA was detected in plasma at a viral load of 15,002 IU/mL. The patient reported consumption of wild-boar meat in the month preceding symptom onset. The purpura resolved spontaneously approximately 10 days after onset, and liver parameters progressively improved, with HEV RNA becoming undetectable at follow-up. Phylogenetic analysis of the patient-derived sequence identified the strain as HEV genotype 3f, belonging to the 3f2 subcluster. The patient-derived sequence showed similarity with European HEV-3f/3f2 human strains and with swine and wild boar strains, supporting a likely zoonotic food-borne origin. Plasma interleukin-6 (IL-6) was elevated at admission during the purpuric manifestation. DISCUSSION: To our knowledge, this is the first Italian report of an HSP-like purpura temporally associated with acute HEV genotype 3f infection. This case highlights that acute HEV infection may be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting with palpable purpura, while emphasizing the exceptional rarity of this manifestation.

content.title: What a highly monitored chikungunya epidemic reveals about preparedness for Europe and beyond.
content.abstract: The 2024-25 chikungunya epidemic in Reunion Island illustrates the challenge of translating early warning into timely public-health action during fast-moving arboviral outbreaks. Despite advanced surveillance, the epidemic accelerated rapidly and placed substantial pressure on primary care. These challenges, together with the complexity of emergency vaccine deployment, highlight the need for anticipatory, integrated preparedness strategies combining surveillance, vaccination, vector control and research.

content.title: A base-editing and auxotrophic selection platform for linking epigenetic regulators to silent biosynthetic gene clusters in Aspergillus nidulans.
content.abstract: Filamentous fungi harbor numerous silent biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), representing an underexplored reservoir of natural products. Chemical inhibition of epigenetic regulators is an effective strategy for activating silent BGCs, but it often lacks specificity and cannot readily link activated clusters to their cognate regulators. Here, we developed a coupled cytosine base editing and auxotrophic selection platform in Aspergillus nidulans to systematically identify epigenetic regulators of silent gene clusters. An sgRNA library targeting 24 core epigenetic regulators was introduced, together with a cytosine base editor, into 21 pyrG-based PKS reporter strains, enabling growth-based selection and direct sgRNA recovery by Sanger sequencing. This screen identified five regulator-cluster activation pairs, including known interactions and two previously uncharacterized mechanisms. Specifically, KdmB represses the AN7084 gene cluster by erasing promoter H3K4me3, whereas Kmt5 silences the cichorine core pks gene through H4K20me3 deposition. This scalable platform enables rapid matching of silent BGCs with their epigenetic regulators and advances chromatin-guided fungal genome mining.

content.abstract: Scientists have discovered a new tick-borne virus in China that causes flu-like illness and may account for previously unexplained cases of fever, fatigue, digestive problems, and low platelet counts. Most patients with ALTNV alone recovered, but coinfections with another dangerous tick-borne virus were linked to more serious complications.
